answer: The trellis multiplier is published, charged in vertex, and raven lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 2900 identities would post 4687 proofs and burn roughly 45 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
